reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading is factually correct: RPC path (put_rpc_custody_columns at L240-267) does not call observe_gossip_data_column and thus does not update observed_column_sidecars cache. However, this is by-design trust boundary differentiation, not a vulnerability. The RPC path updates observed_slashable (via check_columns_for_slashability at L3699), which is the actual anti-equivocation cache tracking (slot, proposer) → block_roots to detect proposer equivocation. The observed_column_sidecars cache serves a different purpose: gossip deduplication to prevent reprocessing the same column on the gossip path. Spec SG-010 INV-003 requires 'anti-equivocation cache MUST be updated' - this refers to slashability tracking, which IS enforced. The trust model (BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json) designates Engine API as semi-trusted/authenticated (JWT), and RPC from local EL is considered a different trust boundary than untrusted P2P gossip. Not updating the gossip deduplication cache for RPC imports is intentional: RPC and gossip are separate code paths with different validation requirements. The claim that 'conflicting columns can coexist' misunderstands the architecture: observed_slashable prevents equivocation; observed_column_sidecars only prevents duplicate gossip processing.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: Spec SG-010 INV-003 requires anti-equivocation cache update, which is satisfied by observed_slashable tracking at check_columns_for_slashability (beacon_chain.rs:3699). Spec SG-006 INV-004 defines gossip deduplication key as (slot, proposer, index), which is separate from anti-equivocation.
